title: Meet 'or': at least one is enough
idea: 'or' joins two conditions into one that is True when AT LEAST ONE is True. Meet it with visible output.

options: at least one of A or B is True
exercises.explanation: 'or' is generous: if either side (or both) is True, the whole thing is True.

exercises.prompt:
What is the value of this?

False or True
exercises.explanation: One side is True, and 'or' only needs one, so the result is True.

exercises.prompt:
What is the value of this?

False or False
exercises.explanation: Both sides are False, so 'or' has nothing True to grab - the result is False.

exercises.prompt:
What does this print?

is_weekend = False
is_holiday = True
if is_weekend or is_holiday:
    print("Day off")
else:
    print("Work")
exercises.explanation: is_holiday is True, and 'or' needs only one True side, so 'Day off' prints.

exercises.prompt: Same code, but both are False. What prints?
exercises.explanation: With both False, 'or' is False, so the else runs: 'Work'.

exercises.prompt: 'or' is True even if only one of the conditions is True.
exercises.explanation: Yes - one True side is enough for 'or'. It is only False when every side is False.

exercises.prompt: Match each 'or' expression to its value.
exercises.explanation: 'or' is True whenever at least one side is True, and False only when all sides are False.
